title: Infosys - L1 SP
author: PRATEEK SINGH RATHORE
body:
Online Assessment

The Online Assessment was conducted on the HirePro platform in the CC Lab and consisted of 4 DSA questions.

The difficulty progression was basically:

Easy → Medium → Hard → Why am I even here?

Question 1 — Easy: A basic array problem with some greedy logic and a little brain usage. Thankfully, my brain was functioning. I solved it in around 5 minutes.

Question 2 — Medium: This one involved prefix sums, array manipulation and greedy thinking. The real problem wasn't coding — it was figuring out what the hell the question wanted. After a lot of struggle, I managed to pass 8/12 test cases.

Question 3 — Hard: Then came the DP nightmare. I tried approaching it with 3 DP states, but at that point my brain was not training. Somehow, I still managed to pass 6/12 test cases.

There was still a fourth question left, but after getting mentally destroyed by the first three, I decided I had seen enough. I switched off my PC and called it a day.

Shortlisting

Considering how my OA went, I was pretty sure my chances were gone.

Then the next evening shortlisted

And the interview was scheduled for the very next day at 4 PM. After waiting at TPO office till eternity I will got my chance around 8PM .

Interview

After that OA, I entered the interview room with just one thought:

“After that OA, nothing can surprise me anymore.”

The interviewer gave me a medium-level DSA problem and around 45 minutes to solve it.

And somehow, with God's grace, I came up with the solution in around 5 minutes.

The interviewer was surprised. So was I.

After that, things became pretty chill. The interviewer went through my resume in detail and asked questions about my projects, technical background and basic CS fundamentals. I was able to answer around 90% of the questions confidently.

I walked out feeling pretty good.

At this point, my brain had already decided:

“Maybe SP L2... ₹16 LPA... not bad.”

Result

Then came the result.

Infosys Specialist Programmer L1 — ₹11 LPA

After the emotional roller coaster of the OA, I was honestly just relieved and happy to finally get placed.

Keep studying and have fun !

title: INFOSYS DSE – HACKWITHINFY INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
author: ANIKET KUMAR
body:
INTRODUCTION

Infosys conducts recruitment through multiple channels, including HackWithInfy, On-Campus Hiring, and Off-Campus Hiring.

I participated in the HackWithInfy recruitment process and was selected for the Digital Specialist Engineer (DSE) profile.

The selection process consisted of 3 rounds:

Round 1 – Online Coding Assessment

Round 2 – In-Person Coding Assessment

Round 3 – Technical Interview

ROUND 1: HACKWITHINFY ONLINE CODING ASSESSMENT

The first round was the HackWithInfy Online Coding Assessment.

There were 3 coding questions, and the total time allotted was 3 hours.

The questions were based on Data Structures and Algorithms and tested problem-solving and algorithmic thinking.

I was able to solve all 3 questions successfully within the given time.

After successfully completing the first round, I was shortlisted for the next stage of the recruitment process.

ROUND 2: IN-PERSON CODING ASSESSMENT

The second round was an in-person coding assessment conducted at the college.

There were 4 coding questions in this round.

My performance was:

Question 1: Solved completely.

Question 2: 6 out of 12 test cases passed.

Question 3: 2 out of 12 test cases passed.

Question 4: I was not able to solve it completely.

I was shortlisted for the Technical Interview for the DSE profile.

This round was conducted in person, so the interviewer was able to observe my problem-solving approach and how I approached the coding problems.

ROUND 3: TECHNICAL INTERVIEW

The technical interview was conducted in person.

I was the first candidate to enter the interview room, so I was a little nervous initially. However, the interview proceeded in a friendly and conversational manner.

1. Tell Me About Yourself

The interviewer started by asking:

"Tell me about yourself."

I introduced myself, talked about my academic background, technical skills, interests, and projects.

2. Project Discussion

After the introduction, the interviewer asked me to explain my project.

I explained the project, including:

Project idea

Workflow

Technologies used

My contribution

Implementation

Backend/frontend interaction

After that, the interviewer asked me several follow-up questions related to my project to check my understanding of the implementation and technologies I had used.

3. Fibonacci Series – Coding Question

The interviewer then asked me to write code for the Fibonacci series.

I implemented the solution using Dynamic Programming (DP).

After writing the code, he asked me to:

Explain the code

Explain the logic

Explain how Dynamic Programming was being used

Discuss the approach

I explained the solution and its logic to the interviewer.

4. Python Questions

Since Python was my preferred programming language, the interviewer asked me several questions related to Python.

The questions were mainly focused on my understanding of Python fundamentals and programming concepts.

This was a good reminder that whatever programming language you mention as your preferred language, you should be prepared to answer questions about its fundamentals.

5. Cloud Computing

The interviewer noticed that I had mentioned a Cloud Computing certification on my resume.

He therefore asked me some questions related to Cloud Computing and my understanding of the concepts covered by the certification.

6. About Infosys

Towards the end of the interview, the interviewer asked me:

"Tell me about Infosys."

I answered by discussing my understanding of the company and its work.

7. My Question to the Interviewer

Finally, the interviewer told me:

"Your interview is done. Do you have any questions?"

I asked him:

"What technology should I learn?"

He suggested that I should pursue more certifications related to Cloud Computing.

The interview then concluded.

FINAL RESULT 🎉

After completing the HackWithInfy recruitment process, I was selected for the:

Infosys DSE – Digital Specialist Engineer
Key Takeaways

Prepare DSA properly for both coding rounds.

Be ready to explain every project mentioned on your resume.

Prepare your preferred programming language thoroughly.

Certifications mentioned on your resume can become a topic of discussion.

Revise the fundamentals of every technical skill mentioned in your resume.

Don't panic if you cannot solve every coding question completely. Focus on your approach and keep trying.

In the interview, communicate your thought process clearly.

Overall, my Infosys HackWithInfy journey consisted of two coding rounds followed by an in-person technical interview, and I was fortunate to be selected for the DSE profile.

author: VIKAS KUSHWAHA
body:
My Placement Experience On Campus , HackwithInfy

I want to share my complete placement experience, starting from the Online Assessments to the final selection.

First Online Assessment — 21 March 2024

My first Online Assessment was conducted from room.

There were 4 coding questions, ranging from medium to hard/advanced level.

I was able to solve 3 questions completely, and all 3 were fully accepted. The 4th question was partially accepted.

Second Online Assessment — Late March 2024

My second Online Assessment was conducted from the college library using the college system.

There were again 4 questions:

The first question was easy and basic.
The second question was medium-level and based on Greedy.
The third question was medium-level and involved Greedy with a simple pattern.
The fourth question was a hard 3D Grid-based DP problem.

I was able to get the 1st and 4th questions fully accepted, while the 2nd and 3rd were partially accepted.

Shortlisting

After around 20–25 days, the shortlisting list was released, and I was shortlisted for the L3 role.

After around 10 days, I had both technical interviews on the same day.

Technical Interview — 28 April 2024

First Technical Round

Generally, the first technical round focused on DSA. Depending on the interviewer and the difficulty of the questions, candidates could get 2–3 DSA questions along with questions from CS fundamentals such as DBMS, CN, Software Engineering, etc.

However, the experience completely depends on the interviewer.

In my case, the interviewer asked me to open my LeetCode profile and checked whether I had solved the question before.

He then gave me a question that was tagged as Medium, but I found it much harder than a typical Medium problem. It was not from any standard DSA sheet.

I first came up with an algorithm and explained my approach to him. Then he asked me to implement it.

After implementing the solution, I got TLE.

He gave me some additional time to optimize it. I came up with an optimization idea and explained it, but my solution was still failing on some test cases.

Then he asked me to find the error myself.

I went through my solution, found the issue, and fixed it.

After that, he told me to wait for the result of the second round.

Overall, I would say my performance in the first round was average from my side. I was able to approach the problem, I wasa able to comes up with optimization and debugging but that was not accepted for all leetcode tescases.

Second Technical Round

The second round started with a short introduction, and then the interviewer directly moved to my project.

We had a detailed discussion about my project for around 8–10 minutes.

He asked questions like:

Why did you build this project?

What problem were you trying to solve?

What challenges did you face?

What is the data flow?

What is the overall pipeline?

How do the different components work together?

After that, he asked me a standard DSA question:

Find the sum of two nodes in a BST equal to a given target.

I explained my approach, and then he asked me how I could optimize the time complexity.

He also asked me about the time and space complexity of some standard algorithms.

There was no implementation in this round because the interview was conducted online.

After DSA, he asked me about how I built a website using AI/prompting. He also asked some questions related to Gen AI and how I had used AI in my projects.

Then he moved to System Design.

He asked me to design a voting machine.

I first explained the HLD and then he asked me to explain the LLD. I suggested two possible LLD approaches and explained them.

Finally, he asked me about the SOLID principles, which I explained.

There was no implementation required in the second round.

Overall, I would consider my performance in the second round excellent from my side. I was comfortable discussing my project, DSA, AI, system design, LLD, and software engineering concepts.

Final Result — 24 June 2024

After around one month, the final result was released.

I was selected for the L1 role.

Overall Experience

My overall journey was:

2 Online Assessments → Shortlisting → 2 Technical Interviews → Final Selection

The biggest thing I learned from this experience is that the interview can vary a lot depending on the interviewer.

In my case, the first round focused more on problem-solving, optimization, and debugging, while the second round covered a much broader range of topics including DSA, CS fundamentals, projects, AI, prompting, HLD, LLD, and SOLID principles.

From my side, the first round was average, while the second round went very well.

Overall, it was a great learning experience and taught me that preparation should not be limited to DSA alone.

title: Infosys On-Campus Placement Experience
author: MRITYUNJAY TIWARI
body:
My Infosys on-campus selection process consisted of two main rounds: a coding/online assessment followed by a technical interview.

Round 1: Coding Assessment

The first round consisted of 4 coding questions arranged in increasing order of difficulty. In my experience, the questions were based on standard and commonly practiced DSA concepts. They were not necessarily based on unusual or unfamiliar topics, but someone who has not practiced enough problems might find them difficult, especially when trying to understand the problem statement and identify the underlying pattern.

I would recommend having a good amount of practice on platforms like LeetCode before the assessment. Rather than focusing only on solving a large number of questions, it is useful to understand common DSA patterns and recognize when to apply them.

Round 2: Technical Interview

After clearing the coding round, there was one technical interview. The interview started with two coding questions, out of which I was asked to solve one. Compared to the coding assessment, these questions were relatively easier, although the problem statement was somewhat lengthy or bit tricky.

After the coding part, the interviewer asked questions about the projects mentioned on my resume, including the technology stack I used and the basic architecture of my projects. Since I had worked with React, I was also asked some basic React concepts such as props, hooks, and their usage.

I was then given a small React-based coding task to write. The interview mainly focused on whether I understood the technologies and projects I had mentioned rather than just knowing definitions.

Preparation Tips

My main advice to future candidates would be:

Practice DSA problems consistently, particularly on platforms such as LeetCode.

Focus on understanding common problem-solving patterns rather than memorizing solutions.

Be thorough with every project mentioned on your resume. Be prepared to explain the tech stack, architecture, your individual contribution, and important implementation decisions.

If you mention a framework such as React, make sure you understand its fundamentals, including components, props, state, hooks, and basic implementation.

During coding rounds, read the complete problem statement carefully and manage your time according to the difficulty of the questions.

When practicing, try to read and understand the problem statement yourself before watching a solution or having someone explain it. If you are following a DSA playlist, it can be tempting to immediately listen to the explanation. However, practicing reading the question independently helps you develop the habit of quickly identifying what the problem is asking, even when the statement is lengthy or worded differently from what you are used to.

Try to solve problems under a time limit occasionally. This helps you become comfortable with understanding the question, forming an approach, and coding within limited time.

Overall, the process gave me a good opportunity to demonstrate both my problem-solving skills and my understanding of the projects and technologies I had worked with.

Online Assessment (OA)

The Infosys OA consisted of 4 DSA coding questions. The questions focused mainly on problem-solving, data structures, and algorithms.

Technical Interview

After clearing the OA, I appeared for the technical interview. The interview covered multiple areas:

Resume-based questions — discussion about my projects, technical skills, and experience mentioned on my resume.
OOPs — concepts such as inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction, encapsulation, and their practical applications.
DBMS — database fundamentals, normalization, keys, transactions, and indexing.
SQL — queries involving joins, aggregation, subqueries, GROUP BY, HAVING, and other basic SQL concepts.
Basic System Design — fundamentals such as client-server architecture, APIs, databases, scalability, and basic design concepts.
